artifacts.synopsis: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Gordon was excommunicated by a PCA Session after his former OPC congregation joined the PCA against his expressed wishes; he contended the PCA Session lacked jurisdiction over him. The SJC majority denied his appeal affirming the excommunication, while a four-member dissent argued the SJC should have ruled the case out of order for lack of jurisdiction and standing, as Gordon never voluntarily became a PCA member.

artifacts.synopsis: Frank J. Smith complained against Northeast Presbytery after Grace Presbyterian Church was dissolved and its members were placed under Presbytery's care. The SJC ruled the complaint in order, sustained it, and returned the matter to Presbytery for adjudication, holding that dissolution did not eliminate Presbytery's pastoral responsibility or Smith's standing in the pending case.
